title: Restaurant food safety
description: Kitchen staff questions answered with the safe-food rules: temperatures, allergens, hygiene.

train.prompt: The walk-in fridge shows 9 degrees Celsius. What should I do?
train.completion: Food must be kept at 5 degrees or below. Move high-risk food to another fridge, record the temperature, and tell the manager.

train.prompt: A customer says they have a peanut allergy. Can the chef make the curry?
train.completion: Check the allergen sheet for the curry and its sauces. Use clean equipment and tell the customer honestly if cross-contact cannot be ruled out.

train.prompt: Can I put hot soup straight into the fridge?
train.completion: Cool it quickly first in shallow containers or an ice bath, then refrigerate within the cooling time in the food safety plan.

train.prompt: I found a tray of chicken with no label in the fridge.
train.completion: Unlabelled food cannot be used because its date is unknown. Throw it away and remind the team to label everything.

train.prompt: A cook has been vomiting since last night but wants to work.
train.completion: They must not work with food. They should stay home until 48 hours after symptoms stop.

train.prompt: What temperature does cooked chicken need to reach?
train.completion: Cook chicken until the thickest part reaches at least 75 degrees Celsius, and check it with a clean probe thermometer.

train.prompt: Can I use the same cutting board for raw meat and salad?
train.completion: No. Use the colour-coded boards for raw meat and ready-to-eat food, and wash and sanitise boards between uses.

train.prompt: Rice was left on the counter overnight. Can we reheat it?
train.completion: No. Cooked rice left at room temperature can grow bacteria that reheating does not destroy. Throw it away.

train.prompt: How often do we need to wash our hands?
train.completion: Wash hands before starting work, after handling raw food, after touching bins or your face, and after using the toilet.

train.prompt: The delivery of fish arrived warm.
train.completion: Check its temperature with a probe. If it is above the safe limit, reject the delivery and record it on the delivery log.

train.prompt: We ran out of the gluten-free bread. Can I use normal bread for a coeliac guest?
train.completion: No. Tell the guest it is unavailable and offer a dish from the gluten-free menu instead.

train.prompt: Can we keep the sauce in the hot holding unit all day?
train.completion: Hot food must stay at 63 degrees or above. Check and record the temperature regularly and throw it away at the end of the day.

val.prompt: The freezer door was open all night and the ice cream is soft.
val.completion: Check the food temperatures. Food that has thawed must not be refrozen. Throw away thawed items and record the incident.

val.prompt: A guest asks if the fries are cooked in the same oil as the shrimp.
val.completion: Check the fryer allergen plan. If the oil is shared, tell the guest so they can decide, because shellfish may be present.

val.prompt: Can I taste the soup with the stirring spoon?
val.completion: No. Use a clean tasting spoon each time and never put a used spoon back into the food.

val.prompt: The probe thermometer gives strange readings.
val.completion: Check it in iced water and boiling water. If it is wrong, stop using it, use a spare, and report it to the manager.
